directoryStems.mcq-ac16b91fc581bb67ba82ac50: בן 88, ללא חסר קוגניטיבי ידוע, אושפז בטיפול נמרץ קרדיולוגי עקב אוטם שריר הלב. בלילה צעק, ניסה לקפוץ מהמיטה ואף הרביץ לאחות שקשרה אותו למיטה. איזה מהבאים נכון בנוגע לטיפול במצב המתואר?
directoryStems.mcq-64427e17545bbfb4d2df9118: בן 84, תשוש בתפקודו, ברקע דמנציה קלה. התקבל למלר"ד עקב חום 38.6, ישנוניות ובלבול. הסטאז'ר הציע לבצע ניקור מותני. מה ההמלצה לגבי ניקור מותני במטופל ?
directoryStems.mcq-1ad50c81f4e5e743efca813b:
בת 94, גרה לבדה עד האשפוז, לא ידוע על ירידה קוגניטיבית. מאושפזת במחלקה פנימית בשל אלח דם (SEPSIS) ממקור של דלקת בדרכי השתן. היא נושאת קתטר שתן ומטופלת באנטיביוטיקה דרך הוריד. רופא גריאטר נקרא לתת יעוץ בשל מצב של אי-שקט ובלבול. בבדיקה נראית כאובה, סובלת מאי שקט פסיכו-מוטורי בולט, ליקוי בקשב, חוסר התמצאות במקום ובזמן. רשימת תרופות שמקבלת:   
 ROCEPHIN  
 ENOXAPARIN (CLEXAN)  
 PARACETAMOL  
 OXAZEPAM (VABEN)  
 RAMIPRIL (TRITACE)  
 TROSPIUM (SPASMEX)  
 BROTIZOLAM (BONDORMIN)  
 מה צריך לייעץ בהתייחס לטיפול התרופתי שהמטופלת מקבלת?
directoryStems.mcq-ce0328117dbe2b4d9dd6b779: לעיתים נדרשת אבחנה מבדלת בין דליריום, דמנציה, דיכאון ופסיכוזה. מה נכון בנוגע להשוואה בין האבחנות השונות?
directoryStems.mcq-13dba157a8b968526f8555b0: בן 85, תשוש בתפקוד, מתגורר לבד, מתהלך עם הליכון, נעזר במטפלת 20 שעות בשבוע. ברקע יתר ל"ד, דיכאון. אין מידע על מצבו הקוגניטיבי או הנפשי טרם האשפוז. אושפז עקב חסימת מעיים, טופל שמרנית עם רזולוציה מלאה של החסימה. הוזמן ייעוץ גריאטרי, כי הכירורג התרשם מבלבול. בשיחה עם החולה – ישנוני, מדווח על מצב רוח ירוד, אינו מתמצא במקום ובזמן, אינו מרוכז במהלך השיחה ועונה תשובות לא רלוונטיות, אינו זוכר פרטים אישיים. מה המאפיין המרמז שמדובר בדליריום ולא בהפרעה אחרת?
directoryStems.mcq-04351e8011b5f96dae499b8d: בת 92 מאושפזת במחלקה אורתופדית יומיים לאחר ניתוח קיבוע שבר ירך בעקבות נפילה. עד הנפילה הייתה ללא ירידה קוגניטיבית ידועה, גרה בבית לבד עם עזרה של מטפלת 15 שעות בשבוע. בנה שהגיע לבקר מצא אותה מדברת עם דמויות אשר לא קיימות בחדר, קוראת לו בשם של אביו אשר נפטר לפני 10 שנים ומנסה לקום מהמיטה. רופא במחלקה מספר שעקב בלבול ואי שקט החולה קיבלה HALIDOL, PHENERGAN ו- VABEN. מה המשך הטיפול במצב זה?
directoryStems.mcq-816b58388ce467ec350c72c3: בת 92, מאושפזת במחלקת אורתופדיה לאחר ניתוח תיקון שבר צוואר ירך. ברקע: דמנציה, מטופלת ב- DONEPEZIL. במהלך הבתר ניתוחי הצוות שמו לב שהיא ישנונית, אינה מתמצאת בזמן או במקום, מתקשה לבצע הוראות של צוות פיזיותרפיה. יש תנודות במצב ההכרה ובמצב הקוגניטיבי במהלך היום. ביום השני לאחר הניתוח – הוצא צנתר משלפוחית השתן. מעקב שארית שתן- ללא שארית. עקב ניסיון לתלוש את העירוי, ידיה של המטופלת נקשרו. אילו מבין הגורמים הבאים תורם לתסמונת ממנה היא סובלת כעת?
directoryStems.mcq-392a084da2a4b39dd0a1eaed: בת 88 פנתה למיון עקב שקיעה במצב ההכרה. לפני שבוע נפלה ונחבלה וסבלה מכאבים קשים. המשפחה יודעת שהחולה לקחה תכשירים שונים לשיכוך כאב, ולאחר מכן הפכה להיות שקועה. המשפחה מביאה שקית עם תרופות אנלגטיות שונות אותן החולה לקחה בבית בשבוע האחרון. מי מבין התרופות האנלגטיות הבאות יכולה לגרום בסבירות גבוהה לשקיעה הכרתית?
directoryStems.mcq-a7ef58ae7e009a3a9ac61661: A 78-year-old man is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three, he becomes agitated, pulls at IV lines, and is disoriented after being oriented that morning. In addition to the acute change, which finding is central to delirium assessment?
directoryStems.mcq-00d77f400146c113ffb896e7: A 75-year-old man with COPD develops confusion and fatigue over 12 hours. His family says he is unlike his usual self. He is inattentive, lethargic, and less active than usual. Heart rate is 88/min, blood pressure 140/85 mm Hg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 92% on home oxygen. Which interpretation and initial approach fit this presentation?
directoryStems.mcq-b32a891064795b871ca183b4: An 82-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with an acute change in mental status. The team applies the Confusion Assessment Method. Which combination satisfies its diagnostic algorithm?
directoryStems.mcq-9eaebe462ab51346d0b6a674: An 85-year-old patient has a 4AT score of 6. Which action addresses the potential causes of the suspected delirium during the initial evaluation?
directoryStems.mcq-46644f55b2fbd697efeaa5d0: An 85-year-old woman after hip-fracture surgery is at risk for delirium. Which intervention is inappropriate for routine prevention and management when alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal is not present?
directoryStems.mcq-31d5726d187e61198ded3224: An older patient presents to the emergency department with acute confusion but no fever. Which principle applies when considering infection?
directoryStems.mcq-014bc0a93fc69d315ebcbd66: An older emergency-department patient becomes quiet and slow after an acute change in mental status. Why can hypoactive delirium go unrecognized?
directoryStems.mcq-b5982eeb5917c3137a99bf22: A 69-year-old woman who was cognitively at her usual baseline until this week develops confusion, disorientation, and agitation over several days. During examination her attention fluctuates and her level of consciousness is clouded. Which syndrome best fits and requires a search for an underlying medical cause?
directoryStems.mcq-0af80d9e5951ed14752b3789: A 76-year-old woman taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation (INR 2.8) develops acute confusion, picks at her clothes, and sees small children in her room. Ciprofloxacin was started three days ago for a UTI. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, pulse 84, blood pressure 142/78 mm Hg, and urine microscopy now shows 0-2 WBC/hpf. Which approach to the new confusion is supported?
directoryStems.mcq-4e3d149ab0a840fa3ae031c9: A 75-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment and recurrent falls develops acute agitation on the second day after hip-fracture repair. She pulls at her Foley catheter and has a positive CAM. Assessment finds no continuing need for the catheter and no immediate threat to safety or essential treatment. Which initial step best follows nonpharmacologic delirium care?
directoryStems.mcq-781def9f349eccefcadc2187: An older man develops delirium during an acute illness. Evaluation identifies several possible contributors, including respiratory disease and medication exposure. Which principle should guide the initial evaluation and treatment?
directoryStems.mcq-f6b3669c5ef6da1d69c00a54: A 77-year-old man with diabetes and stage 3a chronic kidney disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. On the third day he develops new confusion, difficulty following commands and picking at the sheets; his wife reports that he was cognitively clear the day before. Medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, ceftriaxone and as-needed diphenhydramine for sleep. Which approach fits the medication component of delirium management?
directoryStems.mcq-e5b268ef2e0a81d5caeb4c91: A 79-year-old man was cognitively clear before hip-fracture surgery. During one night he develops inattention, disorientation, and hallucinations, with symptom severity changing through the day. Which combination is central to recognizing delirium?
directoryStems.mcq-05c5a4e9b592465450705211: An 84-year-old woman with dementia and pneumonia develops delirium. Despite treatment of contributing factors and nonpharmacological measures, she strikes staff and disrupts essential treatment. An antipsychotic is being considered. Which treatment aim is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-e1691852021214f7e2fdb282: An 85-year-old man develops delirium with inattention and disorganized thinking over one day. He has no fever, head trauma, focal neurologic deficit, or suspected seizure. The initial assessment has not found a cause, but medication review remains incomplete: his daughter provides a partial list including an unidentified sleep preparation. What should be completed next?
directoryStems.mcq-72690290a42b0d9f8e7d1739: An 84-year-old man with renal impairment, reduced fluid intake, and mild dementia develops delirium. He takes morphine and gabapentin and now has hypotension and worsening kidney function. Which approach addresses potentially treatable contributors?
directoryStems.mcq-fc5a641d1fd67fa6d3d259a4: A 79-year-old woman with mild dementia and pneumonia develops delirium after receiving diphenhydramine for sleep. What should the medication assessment consider?
directoryStems.mcq-b6b8e37a69431eee106c8841: A 91-year-old man with mild dementia develops inattention and disorganized thinking within hours. He is stable and has no fever, head trauma, focal neurologic signs, or suspected seizure. After the history and physical examination, which initial evaluation is most appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-aaf72918324cc9c0d0edb406: An 85-year-old man is being evaluated for delirium. A contributing medication has been identified and can be stopped after assessing its benefits and risks. What is consistent with the Hazzard management algorithm?
directoryStems.mcq-89f44e91e99a5812e1bf85ea: An 84-year-old man develops delirium after hip-fracture surgery. He is stable and poses no immediate danger. Oxycodone is prescribed as needed, but his actual doses and pain severity are unclear. What medication-related step is appropriate before deciding on a dose change?
directoryStems.mcq-45c428a96ead52c22f71bb35: A man with established dementia becomes more somnolent and dependent on assistance. Which information about the time course particularly supports superimposed delirium?
directoryStems.mcq-5ef00c1fb1529c65db806330: A 78-year-old man with mild dementia is undergoing rehabilitation after hip fracture surgery. He develops an abrupt change in attention, reduced food intake, and blood pressure lower than usual. What is the appropriate diagnostic approach?
directoryStems.mcq-482ed7152689655c9f5342fb: An 80-year-old woman is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. Evaluation and treatment of the causes are ongoing. Despite nonpharmacologic measures, her behavior threatens her safety and interrupts essential treatment. Which prescribing principle applies?
directoryStems.mcq-baa689278d944175f77ff81b: A woman with dementia takes a sedating medication that was not prescribed for her and develops acute confusion. Evaluation identifies the drug as a harmful contributor. She poses no immediate danger to herself or staff. Which approach follows the delirium management flowchart?
directoryStems.mcq-f2b8a0f0088568d835673a93: A patient with Parkinson disease and cognitive impairment has new agitation and hallucinations. Oxybutynin was added yesterday, after the symptoms had begun. While evaluating delirium, how should the new prescription be managed?
directoryStems.mcq-db9ddda7ac2ee519d3baeac7: An 84-year-old man develops postoperative delirium. He is confused but relatively calm, is not endangering himself, and is not interfering with essential treatment. What is the initial approach to his symptoms?
directoryStems.mcq-da220564b557a7aade08e9a8: An 82-year-old man on the third day after right hemicolectomy develops acute confusion and visual hallucinations of insects on the wall. He has COPD, BPH, and mild cognitive impairment and takes tamsulosin, tiotropium, and aspirin. Temperature is 37.1°C, blood pressure 128/70, heart rate 88, and oxygen saturation 94% on room air. His catheter was removed six hours ago and he has not passed urine. Examination now finds a painful, palpable bladder. Which urinary condition fits this finding during his delirium assessment?
directoryStems.mcq-12b9901d01a57dedbb869a4d: A man receiving chronic benzodiazepine treatment develops delirium after the medication is stopped around surgery. Evaluation establishes a withdrawal syndrome. How does this cause affect the role of benzodiazepines?
directoryStems.mcq-19bcc26548b5f8512045b40e: A 77-year-old woman develops delirium after a procedure. Evaluation and treatment of precipitants have begun. She is restless but is not endangering herself or interrupting essential care. Which approach is appropriate for her symptoms?
directoryStems.mcq-3efe77174f290bfdcd4c7f34: An 82-year-old woman with moderate visual impairment from diabetic retinopathy has been confused for two days. Her family found her using the wrong medication bottles and putting eye drops in her ears. MMSE is 22/30 with orientation and memory errors, and vital signs are normal. Which assessment directly addresses possible delirium?
directoryStems.mcq-d39e7833a7688bd5fb42289b: An 83-year-old woman with wet age-related macular degeneration treated with anti-VEGF injections and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24) develops acute delirium during hospitalization for pneumonia. During evening nursing care she becomes agitated, pulls at her gown, and calls for her deceased husband. She takes ceftriaxone, acetaminophen, and artificial tears. Which initial symptom-management approach is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-2eb43f65da0aecba00a7fa69: An 83-year-old man with severe COPD, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure develops delirium while hospitalized with pneumonia. He was continent and cognitively intact at baseline. A Foley catheter was inserted on admission, but reassessment finds no continuing indication. Which device-related step fits delirium care?
directoryStems.mcq-ba1b912879fbbbce37493164: A 78-year-old woman with stable cognitive impairment develops inattention and fluctuating confusion over several days after starting tolterodine. Evaluation finds no dehydration or metabolic disturbance, and the acute deterioration resolves after the drug is stopped. Which explanation fits?
directoryStems.mcq-9c8a6d3e223cbda36911f861: An 84-year-old woman who lives alone and manages her medications was independent in basic ADLs until three days ago. Her daughter finds her acutely confused and inattentive. Temperature is 37.1°C, heart rate 88/min, blood pressure 108/62 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 20/min. She is oriented to person only and repeatedly asks when her husband, who died two years ago, will arrive. Medications include donepezil 10 mg, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and zolpidem 10 mg nightly, started one week ago. Which interpretation should guide the initial assessment?
directoryStems.mcq-5247ac9361ebd454c1b5a0c4: An 81-year-old woman is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. She has difficulty sleeping at night but is not endangering herself or interrupting essential treatment. Which environmental change is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-98e1cdd5a7cc0e451991737a: A 75-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia has Parkinson disease, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and insomnia. He takes carbidopa-levodopa, tamsulosin, and zolpidem. He develops acute confusion and visual hallucinations, with a positive CAM screen despite stable vital signs and no fever. Which recommendation about zolpidem agrees with the 2023 Beers Criteria?
directoryStems.mcq-62ca0466aaece5402ce7df47: A patient with postoperative delirium continues to endanger himself and interrupt essential treatment despite nonpharmacologic measures. Medication for symptom control is judged necessary. Which prescribing principle should guide treatment?
directoryStems.mcq-76a27dfec1aa6a5d83782683: A 79-year-old woman taking a stable dose of donepezil develops new delirium. Initial blood tests and urinalysis do not explain it. What is the appropriate next step in evaluation?
directoryStems.mcq-a9ae2356d3d02bc98927b82a: An 85-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia becomes disoriented, pulls at his oxygen cannula, and tries to leave bed after 36 hours without sleep. He is oriented to person only. Home medications are tamsulosin, metformin, and lisinopril. Temperature is 37.8 degrees C, pulse 92, blood pressure 135/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate 22, and oxygen saturation 91% on 2 L/min. His daughter says he would want everything done. Which initial supportive approach accompanies evaluation and treatment of his acute illness?
directoryStems.mcq-89aeb9862614a5d1971d95fa: A 77-year-old man hospitalized for a heart-failure exacerbation becomes confused at night, fails to recognize his wife and tries to leave, although he was alert and oriented that morning. His regular drugs are lisinopril, carvedilol and spironolactone; zolpidem was added three weeks ago. Assessment shows acute onset, inattention and disorganized thinking with normal alertness. Which approach addresses a potentially modifiable contributor?
directoryStems.mcq-850edf61e2f74862653cbfb5: A 78-year-old woman develops postoperative delirium. She receives diphenhydramine for sleep and famotidine started during admission; neither has an ongoing essential indication. According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which medication-review approach is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-af1ecb535265e406bb7e4833: An 85-year-old man becomes confused on the second day after total knee arthroplasty. He pulls at his urinary catheter and fails to recognize his family. He has treated hypertension, normal serum chemistry and recent opioid exposure for postoperative pain. No focal neurologic signs or head trauma are found, and the catheter no longer has a clinical indication. Which action fits initial nonpharmacologic delirium management?
directoryStems.mcq-b23b2d149653e7699a123904: An older adult develops delirium on the second day after hip surgery. He receives morphine PCA and metformin despite an eGFR of 22 mL/min/1.73 m². In addition to evaluating infection, hypoxia, retention, metabolic disturbance and pain, which medication plan is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-75c8b91ee216b1bffa22c487: An older woman develops delirium after hip surgery. Alongside evaluation and treatment of medical causes, which environmental approach follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-79730f93e221f40840abb513: An 84-year-old man in rehabilitation after hip surgery develops acute confusion and stops participating in therapy. Renal impairment and electrolyte disturbances are present, and he is receiving an opioid. Which management approach is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-24aeae2b7c99ec7399bd78c1: An 82-year-old woman develops inattention, confusion, and fluctuating alertness after hip surgery. Gabapentin appears on her medication list, but its start date and any recent dose changes are unknown. Which diagnostic approach is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-c95ffa5fdb0f69d4c7360e55: A woman with dementia develops confusion and hallucinations over several days after starting a sleep medication. She poses no danger to herself. What is the appropriate initial approach?
directoryStems.mcq-6a5c61ca8d8c798f6a24f571: A patient with delirium and severe agitation has not improved with nonpharmacologic measures. After assessment, cautious antipsychotic treatment is selected. What is the clinical treatment endpoint described in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-84045a58c6dbb9d528a8b641: An 84-year-old man with dementia develops acute confusion, inattention, and visual hallucinations; his CAM assessment is positive. He is calm, not markedly distressed, cooperates with care, and poses no danger to himself or others. Evaluation for reversible contributors has begun. What is the appropriate initial symptom-management approach?
directoryStems.mcq-5fe45d621ac7720d2b98a24b: An 85-year-old man with dementia, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes develops new confusion and inattention over one day. His family describes a clear change from his usual state. Initial assessment also shows hypotension and deterioration in renal function. Which approach to identifying the causes of delirium is supported by Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-45b58f340222ad48c888ec10: A 78-year-old woman develops CAM-positive delirium after hip-fracture surgery, pulling at her catheter and trying to leave bed. She was independent in instrumental activities before admission. Her medications include oxycodone, famotidine, and enoxaparin; renal function has worsened and sodium is low. Alongside identifying and treating contributors, which care plan follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-83997f722dc1b9394be0face: An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer dementia has become more confused over three days. He lives in assisted living and has a baseline MMSE of 19/30. He accused staff of stealing a wallet later found in his drawer and now reports seeing children who are not present. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Temperature is 36.8 degrees C, BP 140/85, and heart rate 78; urine shows 10-20 white cells and positive nitrites. Which feature most strongly supports delirium superimposed on his baseline dementia?
directoryStems.mcq-cdc4bd32d78c4e6b173974fe: A 79-year-old man develops inattention and fluctuating confusion after starting a new medication. He has no fever, focal neurologic deficit, or dangerous agitation. Evaluation identifies the medication as a possible contributor. Which management principle is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-56773e414e88f3e9f98cd327: An 86-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter and needs help with IADLs.
